name: Chabu
catalog_citation: Kibebe Tsehay Taye. 2015. Documentation and Grammatical Description of Chabu. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. (AAU ETD, https://etd.aau.edu.et/items/349d1225-0ded-4757-9f16-9f08924ea263)
catalog_locator: sec. 5.7 Tone, pp. 112, 117 (5.7.2 Functions of Tone in Chabu)
catalog_quote: As Chabu is a tonal language like its neighbouring Nilo-Saharan languages, in this chapter we present an overview of the tonology of the language. Chabu tone has never been treated. In the present study as well, we present a preliminary analysis of the basic features and roles of Chabu tone system. The detailed and exhaustive description of the Chabu tone system requires further study. Chabu has three level and one contour tones; High, Mid, Low and falling, which dominantly play a lexical function. ... Chabu seems to have only vowels as tone bearing units. Vowel length does not seem to have an effect on the tone melody of the lexeme. ... Monosyllabic words in Chabu are few in number. However, in monosyllabic nouns and verbs of Chabu all the three level (high, mid and low) tones are attested. ... The attested function of tone in Chabu is lexical and the following examples illustrate this…

audit.reasoning: The coding 'tonal' rests on the only full grammar of Chabu (Kibebe 2015, 506-pp AAU dissertation, held as PDF+txt), and the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated section and pages (5.7, p. 112; 5.7.2, p. 117). The dissertation contains no word-stress statement anywhere, and its own review of the earlier primary literature (Anbessa Teferra 1991, 1995) reports that those works also recognize lexical tone. No later or better phonological/prosodic study was found via Glottolog 5.1, Crossref (incl. the 2023 Oxford Handbook of Ethiopian Languages, which has no Shabo chapter), ERIC, or the Wikipedia bibliography; The unheld items (Teferra 1995, 9 pp; Teferra 1991, 17 pp; Aberra n.d. ms) are short, older, print-only or unpublished, and per Kibebe's summary agree on lexic
